recipes.name: Vietnamese pickled carrots and daikon (radish)
ingredients: 2 medium carrots (, peeled cut into 3mm / 1/10" batons (Note 1))
1/2 large daikon (white radish) (, peeled, cut the same as carrots (Note 1))
3/4 cup rice wine vinegar ((sub apple cider vinegar))
instructions: Pickle - In a large bowl, dissolve the salt and sugar in the hot water. Stir in vinegar. Add carrots and daikon - they should just about be covered.
2 hours - Leave for 2 hours until the vegetables are slightly floppy.
Using - Drain well to use, or just take out what you need (no liquid, just the vegetables).
Storing - The vegetables will keep in the fridge for 2 months, in the pickling liquid. Use airtight glass containers or jars (not plastic).

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Carrot and daikon – it’s hard to quantity the amounts but basically you want the same quantity of each, and enough so it is just covered by the pickling liquid. Can’t find white radish? Double up on carrot! In Vietnam I’ve seen mixes with more carrot/less daikon, and vice versa. Use as much as you can as long as the vegetables are just about submerged in the liquid. 2. STORAGE: Keep for 2 months (likely longer!) in an airtight container the fridge submerged in the liquid, like you would any other pickle! Nutrition ESTIMATE per serving. For pickles, I have to make an educated guess for how much sugar and salt is absorbed by the vegetables.
